definitions.gloss: recapture; recovery; taking back by force
definitions.explanation: The act of recovering something that was taken or lost, often implying forceful or determined action. Used in military, sports, and political contexts.

examples.japanese: {領土|りょうど}を{奪還|だっかん}する。
チームは{首位|しゅい}の{座|ざ}を{奪還|だっかん}した。
examples.english: The team reclaimed the top spot.

examples.japanese: {人質|ひとじち}{奪還|だっかん}のための{作戦|さくせん}が{実行|じっこう}された。
examples.english: An operation to recover the hostages was carried out.

notes:
USAGE:
{奪還|だっかん} implies forceful recovery of something important that was lost or taken. It is stronger and more dramatic than {回復|かいふく} (recovery) or {取|と}り{戻|もど}す (to get back).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {領土|りょうど}を{奪還|だっかん}する (to recapture territory)
- {政権|せいけん}を{奪還|だっかん}する (to retake political power)
- {奪還|だっかん}{作戦|さくせん} (recovery operation)
- タイトルを{奪還|だっかん}する (to reclaim a title)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{取|と}り{戻|もど}す is more general and everyday, while {奪還|だっかん} implies something was wrongfully taken and is being recovered through determined effort or force.
